area_overview: Core SQL Server table and DML syntax: data types, CREATE TABLE, GUIDs, foreign keys/cascade, INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, OUTPUT with INSERTED/DELETED, variables, IF/IF EXISTS, @@ROWCOUNT, and TRY/CATCH.
key_ideas: CREATE TABLE defines columns, data types, nullability, identity, keys, and relationships.
SQL Server types include int/bigint/decimal/bit/date/time/datetime2/nvarchar/uniqueidentifier/rowversion and binary types.
uniqueidentifier stores GUID values; NEWID and NEWSEQUENTIALID generate them differently.
Foreign keys can enforce relationships and can define cascade behavior.
INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE can use the OUTPUT clause to return changed rows.
INSERTED and DELETED are logical rowsets available in OUTPUT and trigger contexts.
Variables are batch-scoped and declared with DECLARE; assignment can use SET or SELECT.
@@ROWCOUNT reports rows affected by the previous statement and should be captured immediately if needed.
TRY...CATCH handles T-SQL errors; ERROR_* functions expose details inside CATCH.
THROW is the modern way to rethrow or raise an error after catch/handling.

reading_quality.visual_reading: R04 screenshots are a mixed but coherent core syntax road; P03 MERGE/index/ALTER neighbors were checked and reserved.
limitations: Some screenshots are small code fragments; transcript groups them by syntax family.
P03/R05 will handle MERGE/upsert, transactions, indexes, ALTER TABLE, constraints, and views.
